goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernameForm.java:47 — Calling isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without the now-required UserModel argument makes the services module fail to compile.

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 — Requiring user != null disables conditional passkey form setup for every normal login where no user is selected, regressing the existing passkey login flow.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. The `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` method at line 160 returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. This method is called in `authenticate()` and `challenge()` methods. Looking at the diff, the change in `authenticate()` moves the passkey setup outside the `if (context.getUser() != null)` block, so it now runs for all cases. The condition `user != null` in `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` is intentional - when user is null during normal login, the original code also didn't call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` because it was inside the `if (context.getUser() != null)` block. The new code maintains similar behavior while also enabling passkeys during re-authentication scenarios. The tests in the diff confirm passkey login still works correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:128 — The new hook duplicates shouldDisplayAuthenticators with the same default, forcing subclasses to coordinate two independently overridable methods for one display decision.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a duplicate method 'shouldDisplayAuthenticators' that conflicts with the new 'shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators' method. However, examining the diff, there is no 'shouldDisplayAuthenticators' method shown anywhere. The diff only shows the addition of 'shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators' method in WebAuthnAuthenticator.java and its override in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java. The finding references a method that doesn't exist in the diff, making it a hallucination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/util/AuthenticatorUtils.java:125 — This generic utility now depends on a browser-form constant and mutates login-form attributes, widening an internal constant to public and leaking UI-specific policy across package boundaries.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the constant USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH was changed from protected to public in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java (line 58), and the new utility method setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError in AuthenticatorUtils.java imports and uses this constant (line 35) while also manipulating LoginFormsProvider attributes (lines 127-131). This is a legitimate architectural concern about coupling between a generic utility class and browser-specific form handling. However, this is a design/architecture concern rather than a bug - the code will function correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:115 — Requiring a non-null user before populating conditional-passkey form data removes passkey login from ordinary unauthenticated login pages.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. Looking at the diff, `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is called at line 115, and this method (defined at lines 160-162) returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. However, this is called AFTER the block that handles `context.getUser() != null` (lines 100-113), meaning for unauthenticated users (user == null), the code falls through to line 115. When user is null, `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(null)` returns false, so passkey form data is not filled. But this is intentional - the original code at lines 109-112 also only filled passkey data when `webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` was true AND user was null (inside the `context.getUser() != null` block). The new code actually moves the passkey setup OUTSIDE the user!=null block, and the condition `user != null` in `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` appears to be the intended behavior for conditional passkeys during re-authentication scenarios, not for initial login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:52 — The new conditional-passkey re-authentication error handling has no test that fails a passkey attempt and verifies the username remains hidden and registration disabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new error handling logic in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java at line 52 that calls AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) to handle re-authentication scenarios when passkey authentication fails. While the diff includes several new tests for passkey re-authentication scenarios (webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication, webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication, etc.), none of these tests specifically verify the error case where a passkey attempt fails and checks that the username field is hidden and registration is disabled. The tests focus on successful re-authentication flows. This is a valid observation about missing test coverage for the specific error handling path added in the conditional UI authenticator.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/webauthn/passwordless/PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:294 — Catching any Exception makes the WebAuthn-absence check pass on unrelated Selenium failures instead of verifying the element is absent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at lines 293-298 a try-catch block that catches generic 'Exception' when checking for WebAuthn element absence. The code uses 'driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"))' which throws NoSuchElementException when element is not found. Catching generic Exception instead of NoSuchElementException specifically could mask other Selenium failures (like StaleElementReferenceException, WebDriverException, etc.) and incorrectly pass the test. This is a valid test quality concern - the test should catch NoSuchElementException specifically to properly verify element absence, similar to how it's done in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java line 207 which uses 'Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)'.
